**Author:** Mysticial appears to have written the top answer. A secondary summary of the thread credits "answers by Mysticial" first among the contributors ([caspimind.com](https://caspimind.com/videos/why-sorted-arrays-are-faster/)). I haven't confirmed the vote counts, so treat "top" as likely rather than verified.

**Main explanation:** Branch prediction. The loop's `if (data[c] >= 128)` branch is unpredictable on random data, so the CPU mispredicts often (roughly half the time), and each misprediction flushes the instruction pipeline. Sorted data makes the condition true for one long run and then false for another, so the predictor is almost always right. The question's own text is consistent with this: it's about conditional processing of a sorted versus unsorted array ([stackoverflow.com](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/11227809/why-is-conditional-processing-of-a-sorted-array-faster-than-of-an-unsorted-array)).

Dense sourdough usually comes from a fermentation or handling problem, not the recipe. The most common causes are:

- **Underproofing:** the dough didn't rise enough before baking. This can come from a weak or unready starter, or cold dough.
- **Overproofing:** the dough fermented too long, lost its ability to hold gas, and collapsed or baked flat.
- **Weak shaping:** the loaf spread or lost surface tension during shaping.
- **Incomplete bake:** the loaf was underbaked, or sliced while still hot and gummy.
- **Flour or hydration:** whole grain flour or changed flour/water weights can give a heavier crumb.

**Fixes:**
- Use a starter that has visibly doubled after feeding before you mix.
- Mark the dough's starting level and check growth, rather than relying only on the clock.
- Shape more firmly to build surface tension.
- Bake fully, preheating the oven and Dutch oven well, and let the loaf cool before judging the crumb.

Sources: [How To Make Sourdough, "Why Is My Sourdough Bread Dense?"](https://howtomakesourdough.com/overproofed-sourdough/why-is-my-sourdough-bread-dense/) and the other search results it appeared with, such as [Flourwise](https://flourwise.com/blog/why-is-my-sourdough-dense/).

Note: when I fetched the How To Make Sourdough link, the returned text was from a different site (flexsourdough.com), so the causes above are checked against that text. I didn't verify the rest of the pages in full.
